steps.title: The mine and its last week
steps.say: An invented open-pit copper mine: a block model of 28,800 blocks on six benches, exploration drill holes and blast-hole assays, six shovels on their panels, 28 haul trucks, a crusher with a surge bin, a mill and two stockpiles, after a week of day and night shifts. The models are trained on the first ten shifts and scored on the last four, each against a plain baseline.

steps.title: The orebody and the shift plan
steps.say: Bench 3 as the grade estimator sees it, with the spread of each estimate, the drill holes and the blasts. Shovel S1 is about to start a new blast whose assays are still at the lab, so ore control classifies it from the resource model. The shift starts on the mine's usual plan: trucks split between the shovels by what each needs, ore routed at the cut-offs, the crusher topped up from the stockpiles in proportion.

steps.title: A low-grade zone and three breakdowns
steps.say: The generator is told two things the service will only see through its data: the blast S1 is digging into hides a barren dyke the drill holes missed (true grade at a third, the lab returns the assays two and a half hours in), and three trucks fail: a tyre at 07:10 with no warning, a cooling system at 08:30 and an oil pump at 09:20. Four hours of the shift run on the plan in force.

steps.title: What the data says
steps.say: The crusher's analyser sees the feed grade fall out of the plant's window. The blast-hole assays come back and the estimate under S1 drops: the zone appears on the bench. The engine models flagged two trucks before they failed; the tyre gave no warning. An OEM feed reports engine data for two trucks: one record accepted and scored, one refused.

steps.title: Re-optimise haulage and construct the blend
steps.say: The dispatch MIP re-plans the rest of the shift from where the 25 working trucks are: how many trucks each shovel gets, where each shovel's high- and low-grade ore goes, and how much to reclaim, inside the plant's grade window and arsenic limit at a confidence level. Then the blend optimiser schedules the loader hour by hour, in whole loads, beside a proportional blend on the same pit feed.

steps.title: Compare in the twin, then a second person approves
steps.say: The twin re-runs the remaining eight hours twenty times under the plan in force and under the new plan, on the same random draws: production, fuel, revenue and the economic objective. The engineer proposes the plan with that evidence; their own approval is refused; the shift supervisor approves and it is dispatched.

steps.title: The rest of the shift
steps.say: Eight more hours run under the approved plan: the plant's hours against the window and, from the generator, what the baseline plan would have done on the same randomness. Then the audit trail.
